subject: Problem with "different set of observed variables" and likelihood function

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Problem with "different set of observed variables" and likelihood function
parts:
Hi all,

I have encountered an anomalous problem in lavaan (0.5-22, R 3.3.2 on Mac) with the likelihood function becoming substantially worse with the addition of variables. When comparing nested models (where one has more predictors than the other), I receive the warning: In lavTestLRT(object = <S4 object of class "lavaan">, SB.classic = TRUE, : lavaan WARNING: some models are based on a different set of observed variables." I looked at the parTable for each model but don't see anything peculiar. And I ran both models in Mplus and got rather different results (with the model with more predictors having a higher LL, as expected). I initially thought that perhaps the regressors were being treated as endogenous in one case, but this did not seem to be the case in the parTable (variances and intercepts have exo==1). Thanks in advance for any advice you can offer.

Best wishes,
Michael

--

#this is the first model
simple2 <- "
large_self_coupling_patient ~  iip_elcpt
large_self_coupling_partner ~ iip_elcpr
large_cross_coupling_patient ~ iip_elcpt
large_cross_coupling_partner ~ iip_elcpr
"

simple2_m <- sem(simple2, datClean2, missing = "listwise", estimator = "ML", mimic="Mplus", meanstructure = TRUE)

#this is the second model
simple3 <- "
large_self_coupling_patient ~  iip_elcpr + iip_elcpt + pdcountcpt + pdcountcpr
large_self_coupling_partner ~ iip_elcpr + iip_elcpt + pdcountcpt + pdcountcpr
